bucket; `SourceMaps` is how a reader is handed the maps of its snapshot's
  handle. A reader takes the map only when it is `ramped`, so a constant
  clip keeps today's arithmetic exactly. `rate` is the core's rate profile
  (`RatePoint`s, SR-26), checked on decode; a list that fails the check is
  [] and the map is kept. `TimelineView+SourceMap.swift` is
  the filmstrip's and the waveform's map-aware `sourceTime`
  (`TimelineView.swift` is frozen; it holds only `sourceMaps`, set in
  `refreshTimeline` from the same handle as the snapshot).

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**The editor.**
- `EditorWindowController.swift`, `WelcomeWindowController.swift`,
  `AppDelegate.swift` (+`Menus`, +`ClipMenus` — the Clip menu's submenus, Add
  Background, Transition, Motion, Look and Label, a pure move out of `+Menus`,
  grading GR1 — +`Recording`, +`Updates` — Frame Job ▸ Check for Updates…
  and the Sparkle updater, compiled only under `FRAMEJOB_UPDATER`
  (Distribution, spec §11 PUB-6..PUB-9) —, +`GraphicMenu` — the Insert
  menu's builder (Adjustment Clip first, then Graphic ▸), File's three graphic-file items (`addGraphicFileItems(to:)`,
  called once from `fileMenu()` right after Add Image to Graphics…: a
  separator, then Rename Graphic…, Delete Graphic… and Restore Graphic
  Version…, no key equivalents, spec §11 G-30) and Help ▸ Graphics
  Reference, `showGraphicsReference`, on the delegate — +`Tutorials` — Help ▸
  Tutorials ▸ Open Practice Project, spec §11 TU-6, TU-7; TU3 adds the
  per-page submenus above it), `main.swift` — the window,
  the no-document window, the launch/terminate flow and the whole menu bar
  (spec §9). Menu items are nil-target selectors down the responder chain.
  `AppDelegate.swift` binds the agent socket at launch, then calls
  `ProjectDocumentController.complainUnlessShared()`, and releases the
  socket at quit. Copy MCP Command is Settings' MCP pane's (`MCPSettingsPane.swift`,
  spec §11 MC-7); there is no Tools menu.
  `main.swift` calls `CodecLibraries.probeIfAsked()` straight after
  `DecoderSupport.enable()` (it prints the bundled encoders' versions and
**Inspector.**
- `InspectorTab.swift` — `InspectorTab` (Clip, Media, Document, Assistant; the
  raw value is the strip index) and the three kind tests the Clip tab's
  sections are chosen by; a pure move out of `InspectorPane.swift` (road map
  12 A2) before `assistant` was added.
- `InspectorNameField.swift` — a pure move out of `InspectorPane.swift`:
  the one-line name field, drawn by `InspectorNameFieldCell` as the value
  field is (spec §11 SH-3); its placeholder is kept off the cell, which draws
  it at rest and under an empty field editor, so the field editor draws none
  (#199).
- `InspectorLabels.swift` — a pure move out of `InspectorPane.swift` (speed
  ramps SR5-0): the small labels and fields every section uses,
  `InspectorRowLabel`, `InspectorMixedBadge`, `InspectorTimecodeField`,
  `InspectorNoteLabel` and `InspectorTextArea` (whose text view routes K-2's
  Return, applying by handing first responder to the content view, K-4).
  `InspectorNoteLabel(wraps:)`
  with `wraps: true` is the one wrapping note: Motion's zero-duration note,
  Speed's silent-audio note and the Clip tab's matte note (#358).
- `InspectorViewController.swift` (frozen: the tab strip, and the PINNED
  container between it and the scroll view that hosts a pane's
  `pinnedBlock`, one generation retired like the strip; the FOOT container
  under the scroll view, collapsed at priority 1 like the pinned one, which
  hosts `refusalStrip`, and the first line of `refresh(isLive:)` that
  clears a stale refusal; `selectClipSubTab`
  is a sub-tab pick's one refresh, and `refresh(isLive:)` calls
  `ClipPane.forgetSubTab()` whenever the selection's ids change, spec §11
  CI-5; a changed selection switches to Clip only from the Media and
  Document tabs, never from the Assistant tab, and `clipPicked()` from any,
  spec §11 AI-14; `onAssistantView` hands the editor the Assistant tab's view;

  as the root's last subview, spec §11 AI-19)
  · `InspectorClipView.swift` (the inspector scroll view's clip view,
  installed first: a width change re-lays its document view, so a pane follows
  an autohiding legacy scroller, #142) · `InspectorRefusalStrip.swift` (spec
  §11 CI-10: "Refused: " and the
  core's sentence verbatim, remembered with the `editedProject` handle it
  was shown under and cleared on the first refresh under another handle or
  a click; `showRefusal` is the editor's forward of
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse`) · `InspectorTabBadge.swift` (spec §11 AI-19: the
  start minus its offset, floored and head-trimmed through the voices'

  `set_video`, read back.

**Tutorials.**
- `TutorialTargets.swift` — the spotlight target table (spec §11 TU-2 (6)):
  the fixed target names, every `InspectorSection` id with its home (tab,
  sub-tab), the clip references and `manifest()`. Only
  `tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift` calls it until TU3 resolves names to
  views; `tutorial_check.py` holds the table to the `id:` literals in

  test` fails**. The tutorials themselves are the guide's
  (`docs/guide/*.md`), extracted into `Contents/Resources/Tutorials.json` by

  (`tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py`).
- `TutorialClipFacts.swift` — the clip filter's five keys answered per clip
  (spec §11 TU-2 (3): `has_sound`, `has_pixels`, `kind`, `follows_clip`,
  `has_transition`) and `matches`; the probe prints them for the practice
  project and TU2's runner reads `needs` through it.
- `PracticeProject.swift` · `ProjectDocument+PracticeMedia.swift` — the
  practice project (spec §11 TU-6, TU-7): locate, read and open the bundled
  `Practice Project.framejob` as an untitled copy named "Practice Project",
  `isInsideApp(_:)` (what `open_project` refuses and the controller
  redirects), the bundled-media queries, and the save funnel's destination
  record (`noteDestination` / `destination` / `clearDestination`, set in
  `+CacheSaves`, which also clears a lingering `displayName` once the copy
  has a file). `+PracticeMedia` overrides `write(to:ofType:for:originalContentsURL:)`:
  every write but autosave-elsewhere copies the bundled files the copy uses
  into the package's `media/` and writes `project.json` relinked to them,
  so a saved copy never points into the app. The open copy keeps playing
  the bundle's files until it is reopened.

**The agent.**
- `AgentServer.swift` (frozen) and `AgentServer+Project` / `Clips` / `Properties` / `Actions` / `Tracks`
  / `Media` / `Render` / `Export` / `ExportResult` / `History` / `Silence` / `Captions` / `Audio` /
  `Background` / `Scope` / `Transitions` / `CloudCaptions` / `Recording` /
  `Graphics` / `Scopes` / `Destinations`
  (+`RecordingArguments`, +`RecordingResult`, +`RecordingLanding` — the
  landing, `awaitGestureEnd` and `land`; +`RecordingSentences` — the
  error and timeout sentences; +`RecordingChrome` —
  `RecordingToolChrome`, the tool's status item, flipped by the recorder's
  `pauseDidChangeNotification` and frozen at its
  `finishingDidBeginNotification`; +`RecordingCamera` — `record_screen`'s
  `add_speed_ramp`; their answers gain `captions_retimed` and
  `captions_removed` (spec §11 SR-27).
- `AgentServer+Grading.swift` — the grading tools' handlers: `add_adjustment_clip`
  (spec §11 GR-6), mirroring Insert ▸ Adjustment Clip.
- `AgentServer+DevTools.swift` — the dev tools' seam (road map 11, spec
  §11 V-1/V-2): the handler table, catalog rows and off-main set compiled
  only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`, which Debug and Release set and
  Distribution does not. The frozen file merges them (`withDevHandlers`, a
  union) and `catalogJSON()` splices the rows in BEFORE the file tools. It
  holds `devToolsMarker`, the string `tools/proof/dist_check.py` requires in
  Release's binary and absent from Distribution's, and absent from each
  bundle's assistant helper (D12, D13); a tool NAME cannot be the
  marker, because an `-O` binary stores a literal of 15 bytes or fewer
  inline. Its tables hold
  `snapshot_ui` (V2a), `perform_menu_item` and `cancel_sheet` (V2b),
  `select_inspector_tab` (V3), `assistant_send` and `assistant_answer`
  (road map 12 A1), `play_preview` (#127, G-36) and `graphic_memory` (G-37); a dev tool is counted apart from the product tools (`tools/proof/dev_tools.py`).
- `AgentServer+PlayPreview.swift` — `play_preview` (dev only, wholly under
  the flag; spec §11 G-36, §7.9c): plays a window's preview forward through
  the transport's own `setRate` and `seek(to:)` (an optional `seek_to` half

  composed per key, compose milliseconds and, when asked, each frame's
  digest. `stale_ticks` (with `seek_to`, #329) reports those ticks to

  own step or, with `stale_armed`, once a frame in the seek's first

  2)`); `stale_reached` answers the ticks reported. Its four refusals are
  read before the first hop to main. `tools/proof/playback_prefetch_proof.py`

- `AgentServer+GraphicMemory.swift` — `graphic_memory {pressure?}` (dev
  only, wholly under the flag, off main; spec §11 G-37): the graphic
## Rules

**Placement.** New feature = small model/value file + VC extension file +
gesture session struct (`ClipDragSession`, `TrimSession`, `CanvasSession` are
the template): one stored property on the view, logic in the feature's file.
Closures assigned in `loadView` are one-line forwards to named methods — no
business logic in closure bodies. New files are capped at 400 lines; a file
at the ~600-line cap gives something up first, as a pure move landed alone.

**Undo and dirty tracking.** All document mutation flows through
`ProjectDocument`'s entry points — `applyEdit`, `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)`
and the `beginLiveEdit`/`updateLiveEdit`/`endLiveEdit` trio for gestures.
`registerUndo` appears nowhere outside `ProjectDocument`. It overrides
`updateChangeCount` to drop AppKit's automatic counting; the entry points
count deterministically via `countEditChange()`. **Pitfall:** undo
registrations outside an AppKit event (agent edits, async callbacks) land in
the implicit event group AppKit never closes, silently merging edits into one
undo step; any off-event path goes through
`ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit`. It opens its explicit group only for an
`.applied` answer (`commitEdit`, shared with `applyEdit`), so an identity, a
refusal or an error leaves the stack — redo included — untouched (#59).
`endLiveEdit(_:cancelled: true)` is the cancel path (Esc during a canvas
drag, `PreviewCanvasView.onLiveCancel`): it puts the `beginLiveEdit` snapshot
back and registers nothing, with no change count.
**Do not "flush" the manager to grouping level zero** to close that group: the
undo checkpoint `NSDocument` posts inside every save then raises, the
exception is swallowed inside the file coordinator, and ⌘S and `save_project`
hang for good.

**A refusal is the CORE's sentence, and nothing on this side writes one.**
An op answers `.applied`, `.identity` or `.refused` (`ReelEdit.swift`); a
person hears a beep for both non-applied arms and, for a refusal, reads the
core's sentence verbatim after "Refused: " at the inspector's foot (spec
§11 CI-10), and an agent hears
`<Action> made no change: the project is already in that state.` or
`<Action> was refused at <op>: <the rule's own sentence>`, written once in
`AgentServer.performGroupedEdit`. **No handler applies an op to see what
would happen and then writes its own reason**, and none re-derives a rule's
arithmetic to predict one. Spec §11's **D2-1** is the line: a check that
predicts a RULE goes, a check that names the CALL stays — an argument a
handler cannot read or was not given (`AgentServer+Arguments.swift`), or a
composite's own reading, like `normalize_clip` with nothing it could
MEASURE. Prose that TEACHES a rule before the call belongs in a tool
description; prose that explains a refusal after it is the core's to write.

**Two callers swallow a refusal on purpose.** `ReelProject.scoped(_:)` drops
the core's message because every caller is a VIEW asking about view state
`clampViewState` has already cleared, so a nil is a race with an undo and
not a failure to report. `ProjectDocument.updateLiveEdit` swallows every
answer but `.applied` because a refused tick is NORMAL mid-drag — the edge
is past a neighbour for a moment — and recovers on the next one with the
last good frame still on screen, where a drag that spoke would interrupt the
gesture to say what the person is already fixing with the mouse;
`endLiveEdit` then registers no step at all. Neither is a gap to be closed
(kpgalligan/framejob#8's eighth decision).

**Lenient decoding is for what the CORE wrote; nothing a caller wrote is
decoded through it.** `ProjectSnapshot`/`MotionProps`' `lenient` and
`nullable` exist so a project, plan, recipe or export setting a NEWER build
wrote still opens — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, an unreadable
value a default or a clear. Run over an agent's own object that same
leniency is a silent correction, so a caller-authored object (a patch, a
colour, a region, a new clip's text or shape) goes to the core unread
through `rawPatchArg` and the RAW factory beside its typed one, and the core
names the dotted path and the value it refused. A scalar enum ARGUMENT
parsed by name is not this (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an
action's `curve`, `set_transition`'s `kind`): what the rule forbids is decoding a caller's
object through a lenient type, and the ONE caller-authored object the app
still reads by hand is `add_media`'s descriptor, which is a media row rather
than a patch and has no op of its own to be refused by
(`AgentServer+Media.swift`'s `mediaDescriptor`, named here so it is an
exception on purpose). The hand checks this rule replaced were deleted
rather than moved, so a new door that wants one is a door that has not been
read; the spec says the same in §7.9, and what went and what it measured is
`archive/roadmap-7.md` §2–§3.

catalog entry declaring `scope`, and a comment naming the UI path. Handlers
follow the canonical shape: `target(a)` → validate ids → `performGroupedEdit`

is a decision: Preview Quality, the preview window, Show Ungraded and the

stops before SILGen, so `closure captures 'x' before it is declared` and its
kin never appear; declare captured copies at the TOP of their scope, and
prove a build with `make app-debug`, and Release with `make app` at the gate.

## Rules

gesture session struct (`ClipDragSession`, `TrimSession`, `CanvasSession` are
the template): one stored property on the view, logic in the feature's file.

business logic in closure bodies. New files are capped at 400 lines; a file
at the ~600-line cap gives something up first, as a pure move landed alone.

`ProjectDocument`'s entry points — `applyEdit`, `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)`
and the `beginLiveEdit`/`updateLiveEdit`/`endLiveEdit` trio for gestures.

`updateChangeCount` to drop AppKit's automatic counting; the entry points
count deterministically via `countEditChange()`. **Pitfall:** undo
registrations outside an AppKit event (agent edits, async callbacks) land in
the implicit event group AppKit never closes, silently merging edits into one
undo step; any off-event path goes through
`ProjectDocument.performGroupedEdit`. It opens its explicit group only for an
`.applied` answer (`commitEdit`, shared with `applyEdit`), so an identity, a
refusal or an error leaves the stack — redo included — untouched (#59).
`endLiveEdit(_:cancelled: true)` is the cancel path (Esc during a canvas
drag, `PreviewCanvasView.onLiveCancel`): it puts the `beginLiveEdit` snapshot
back and registers nothing, with no change count.

and the chat settings are the person's, spec §11 AI-8, AI-11, AI-20) and
Settings' MCP pane (copies a line, edits nothing, MC-7) and Settings'
Playback pane (Background render, the person's setting, spec §11 G-38) get no
mirror, because they edit no project and `set_selection` / `export` already are the capability.
Opening System Settings at a grant's pane (the recorder panel) is no edit
and gets no mirror; `record_screen` refuses by name instead (spec §11
recording).

**State flow.** Views → VC through `on*` closures (`[weak self]`); document →
observers via `.projectDocumentDidChange` with `userInfo["isLive"]` — live
gestures pass `isLive: true` and observers skip expensive reloads
mid-gesture. VC → views is direct property assignment.

**Tracking areas.** `updateTrackingAreas` removes only the view's OWN areas —
`for area in trackingAreas where area.owner === self` — never
`trackingAreas.forEach(removeTrackingArea)`: tooltips are tracking areas owned
by `NSToolTipManager`, and nothing reinstalls one that is removed.

**Popups.** A popup built from model objects carries the object in
`representedObject` and is read from `selectedItem`, never by index, and its
rows are `NSMenuItem`s: `addItem(withTitle:)` REMOVES an existing row with the
same title. `menu.autoenablesItems = false` comes before disabling a row. An
`OptionPopupControl` over model values takes them through the typed init
(`OptionControls+Choices.swift`: `choices:` of title and value, `read` and
`write` in values), not the index init with a hand-kept array beside it.

**Hygiene.** No storyboards/xibs. No `!` force-unwraps, `as!`, or `try!`;
implicitly-unwrapped optionals only for post-`loadView` view refs. Every
non-NSCoder class: `@available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder:)
{ fatalError("<Type> does not support NSCoder") }`. `[weak self]` in retained
closures, never `unowned` (the one deliberate strong hold:
`ScreenRecorder+CameraPrepare.swift`'s prepared start completion keeps its
`PreparedCamera`, so a start that comes first can join it). Main-thread AppKit. **`async`/`await` is allowed
only inside `MediaImporter.swift`** (AVFoundation's loading API is
async-only) **and `SpeechEngine.swift`** (spec §11 W-8: `SpeechAnalyzer`
is async-only; every caller gets a synchronous wrapper or a main-queue
completion, and `Task.detached`, never `Task {}`). Nothing else earns the
exception by asking — screen recording has a complete callback API and
uses it. **`import Synchronization` is allowed only inside `LevelMeter.swift`**,
whose `publish` runs on the audio render thread where a lock invites priority
inversion and `main.async` allocates; every other cross-thread value is an
`NSLock`, the cache ledger's `NSCondition`, the prefetch's `NSCondition`, or
a main hop. `DispatchQueue`
only at the documented seams: the
compositor's render queue, the composition rebuild, import, the cache lane's
queue (`MediaImporter.CacheLane`, spec §11 #367), the export
progress timer, the AV1 encode queue (`ExportEncodePump`'s
`com.kgalligan.framejob.export.encode`, with its `DispatchSemaphore(3)` between the
video pump and the encoder, spec §11 CX-12), the WebM writer's two pump queues
(`com.kgalligan.framejob.export.webm.video` and `.audio`, CX-15), `Transcriber`'s serial queue, `CloudTranscriber`'s serial
queue and the AssemblyAI client's delegate `OperationQueue` (spec §11's
R6-7), the transcribe sheet's Download row's KVO main hop
(`DispatchQueue.main.async` from `Progress`'s `fractionCompleted`
observation), `FFmpegRewrap`'s serial queue, the container rewrap's per-input writer
queues (`ContainerRewrapWriter.swift`), the one-frame render
queues (`eyedropperQueue`, `frameGrabQueue`, `LookGallery.queue` — a fourth one-frame render joins
this entry rather than growing the list), `ScreenRecorder.shareableContent`'s
global hop, `GraphicStore`'s serial queue (its file-system sources'
handlers, the coalesced pass and the outbox; main publishes through
`drain()` and never waits on it but by `queue.sync`), the cache's main
hop, the alert queue's main hop (`ProjectDocument+Alerts.swift`), the agent lane's per-document serial queues (`AgentLane.swift`), the
assistant session's write queue (`AssistantSession.swift`), the alpha rows'
straightening and the 8-bit rounding (`ExportStraightAlpha.swift`,
`ExportStraightAlphaHalf.swift`, `DispatchQueue.concurrentPerform` over rows,
inside the video pump), and the spend-month
queue (`AssistantSpendMonth.queue`, Settings' ledger fold, answered by a
main hop), the waveform tap's main hop (`WaveformTaps.finished` →
`DispatchQueue.main.async`, from Metal's completion thread), the camera
recorder's two (`CameraCapture.sessionQueue` — one static queue shared by
every capture — for the configuration lock, `startRunning`, `stopRunning`
and the unlock; `CameraCapture.sampleQueue`, the data output's delegate queue
and the only place the armed writer and the warm-up are touched), the screen
frame watch's sample handler queue (`ScreenFrameWatch.queue`, the `.screen`
output's, with everything it shares with main under its `lock`; CAM-9), and — not a
queue but a seam all the same — the graphic
prefetch's worker `Thread`s (`GraphicPrefetch.swift`, G-26, G-36), and the
graphic browser's preview player — one `Thread` per player
(`GraphicPreviewPlayer.swift`, G-45) and its `DispatchQueue.main.async`
frame hop, and the browser's export `Thread`
(`com.kgalligan.framejob.graphic-export`, G-46), and Help ▸ Tutorials ▸
Open Practice Project's one `DispatchQueue.main.async { NSApp.presentError }`
hop (`AppDelegate+Tutorials.swift`, so the item's menu verdict stays
`window`; spec §11 TU-6). `tools/practice/practice_media.swift`'s two writer
queues are a dev generator's, not the app's. Beyond the camera's
two and the frame watch's, the recorder adds NO queue of its own:
framework callbacks are stamped where they land and hopped to main. Colors,
fonts and metrics come from `DS` tokens; shared controls go in
`Controls.swift`. **A refusal and an identity both beep** (`NSSound.beep()`)
and neither makes an undo step — that is what makes a person's experience of
the two alike, and it is deliberate (spec §5.5); a refusal ALSO shows its
sentence at the inspector's foot (CI-10), the one difference a person
sees; only invalid input throws, and errors never crash.
4-space indent, ~100 columns.

**`make typecheck` is authoritative for TYPE errors, and only those.** It
stops before SILGen, so `closure captures 'x' before it is declared` and its
kin never appear; declare captured copies at the TOP of their scope, and
prove a build with `make app-debug`, and Release with `make app` at the gate.

**Debug and Release.** The loop and mutant tiers build and drive a Debug app
(spec §11 V-4, V-5); the gate builds Release and the run a phase records is on
Release. (a) The 18 `assert`/`assertionFailure` sites are live in Debug: a trap
is a defect to fix, never an assert to delete or a reason to switch
configuration. (b) Debug is unoptimised: a proof that measures time or
throughput is `release_only`, as is one that needs a TCC grant. (c) A failure
only Release shows is found by the recorded run and fixed in that phase.

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Tutorials TU1 and TU1b — the guide's tutorials checked against the app and the bundled practice project (spec §11 TU-2, TU-7). A line of `make test`; no app instance, no key. python3 tools/proof/tutorial_check.py # the guide (make test) python3 tools/proof/tutorial_check.py --facts FILE # against saved facts, no build python3 tools/proof/tutorial_check.py --save-facts FILE # also write the probe's facts python3 tools/proof/tutorial_check.py --selftest # CONTROL + 19 mutants Every page of `docs/guide/` is parsed by `tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py` (the build step's own parser: structure, JSON, ids unique), then each tutorial is checked against TU-2's closed vocabulary and the app's facts, which `tutorial_probe.swift` prints — compiled over `app/Sources` with `-D FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` through `swift_build.py`'s `build()`, reused when every input is byte-identical: the prepared catalog (a `show_me` tool, its argument keys, an `enum` value), the dev tools' names (refused), the target table (`TutorialTargets.manifest()`: spotlights, a `reveal`'s tab, sub-tab, section and home), the built menu bar (a sentence's bold `A ▸ B` and a menu Show Me, whose leaf's selector must be a key of `capture_spike/inventory.json`'s `selectors`) and a fixture project's clips (a `changed` path and a patch's leaves). The table's section ids are also compared, both ways, with the `id: "", title:` literals in `app/Sources`. The practice project (TU-7): the probe also reads `app/Resources/Practice/Practice Project.framejob` (its second argument) through a fresh `ProjectDocument` and `PracticeProject.read(into:from:)`, the open path's own read, and answers each clip's `TutorialClipFacts` and each media's resolved path. `check_practice` then fails a tutorial whose `needs.clip` no practice clip matches (naming the tutorial), a media that does not resolve inside the package's `media/`, a clip whose keys are not the filter's, a practice read that failed, and every file that drifts from `app/Resources/Practice/SHA256SUMS` or a package over 4,000,000 bytes (`tools/practice/make_practice.py`'s `sums_problems`). Prints `FAIL [ tutorial ][ step ]: ` per problem, then `tutorial_check: tutorials, steps,

problems`; exit 0 iff P is 0. A probe that does not build or answer is a scored FAIL (exit 1), never a skip. `--selftest` copies `tutorial_fixtures/` (a page using every vocabulary key, the facts in miniature with a practice block, an inventory, a sources folder, a stand-in practice folder with its `SHA256SUMS`) into `work/tutorial_check/selftest//` and requires CONTROL to show 0 problems, then each of the 19 mutants (`MUTANTS`, one per refusal class) exactly one problem, naming its page, tutorial and step (and, for a duplicate id, its line). No build. """ import argparse import json import re import shutil import sys from pathlib import Path HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent ROOT = HERE.parents[1] sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE)) sys.path.insert(0, str(HERE / "graphics_spike")) sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools" / "tutorials")) sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools" / "practice")) import bounded # noqa: E402 import swift_build # noqa: E402 from make_practice import PACKAGE_NAME, sums_problems # noqa: E402 from tutorial_extract import Problem, parse_guide # noqa: E402 GUIDE = ROOT / "docs" / "guide" INVENTORY = HERE / "capture_spike" / "inventory.json" SOURCES = ROOT / "app" / "Sources" PRACTICE = ROOT / "app/Resources/Practice" FIXTURES = HERE / "tutorial_fixtures" WORK = HERE / "work" / "tutorial_check" PROBE_SWIFT = HERE / "tutorial_probe.swift" WALL_BUILD, WALL_RUN = 900, 300 TABLE_PAGE = "TutorialTargets.swift" SUMS_PAGE = "SHA256SUMS" KINDS = ("media", "still", "image", "text", "shape", "graphic", "nest", "adjustment") FILTER_KEYS = ("has_sound", "has_pixels", "kind", "follows_clip", "has_transition") STEP_KEYS = ("reveal", "spotlight", "wait", "show_me", "optional") WAIT_KEYS = ("selection", "changed", "clips", "playhead", "range", "sheet", "export_started", "playing") REFS = ("$selection", "$created") PLAIN_VARIABLES = ("$selection", "$created", "$playhead") PATCH_GROUPS = {"set_video": "video", "set_audio": "audio", "set_text": "text", "set_shape": "shape"} LITERAL = re.compile(r'id: "([^"]+)", title:') BOLD = re.compile(r"\*\*(.+?)\*\*") ARROW = "▸" class ProbeFailed(RuntimeError): pass # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # The probe. def build_facts() -> dict: """The probe's answer; raises ProbeFailed when it does not build or answer.""" probe_dir = WORK / "probe" probe_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) entry = probe_dir / "main.swift" source = PROBE_SWIFT.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if not entry.exists() or entry.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != source: entry.write_text(source, encoding="utf-8") binary = probe_dir / "tutorial_probe" sources = swift_build.app_sources() print(f"probe: {len(sources)} sources through swift_build (up to {WALL_BUILD} s)…", flush=True) try: built = swift_build.build(sources=sources + [entry], output=binary, defines=["FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS"], timeout=WALL_BUILD) except swift_build.SwiftBuildFailed as error: raise ProbeFailed(f"the probe did not build: swiftc " f"{error.rc if error.rc is not None else 'before running'} " f"(expired {error.expired}): " + " | ".join(error.diagnostics[:6] or ["(no output)"])) from None print("probe: up to date" if built.reused else f"probe: built in {built.seconds:.0f} s", flush=True) runs = WORK / "runs" shutil.rmtree(runs, ignore_errors=True) runs.mkdir(parents=True) ran = bounded.run([str(binary), str(runs), str(PRACTICE / PACKAGE_NAME)], WALL_RUN, cwd=str(probe_dir), env=bounded.child_env()) if ran["expired"]: raise ProbeFailed(f"the probe ran past {WALL_RUN} s and was killed") for line in ran["stdout"].splitlines(): if line.startswith("ANSWER "): facts = json.loads(line[len("ANSWER "):]) if "error" in facts: raise ProbeFailed(f"the probe answered an error: {facts['error']}") return facts raise ProbeFailed(f"the probe printed no answer (exit {ran['rc']}): " f"{ran['stderr'].strip()[-400:]}") # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # The vocabulary.

"""The dev tools (road map 11, spec §11 V-1..V-3; road map 12 A1), named once
for every proof.

A dev tool is compiled only under `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` (Debug and Release, never
Distribution), so a Release catalog holds the PRODUCT tools plus these and a
Distribution one holds the product tools alone. A script that asserts an exact
set of tools subtracts `DEV_TOOLS` first; `op_argument_proof.py` counts them
apart.

`DEV_TOOLS` is in catalog order: `devTools()` in `AgentServer+DevTools.swift`
splices its rows in immediately before `import_media`, the first file tool:
`snapshot_ui` (road map 11's V2a), then `perform_menu_item` and `cancel_sheet`
(V2b), then `select_inspector_tab` (V3), then `assistant_send` and
`assistant_answer` (road map 12 A1), then `play_preview` (issue #127, spec §11
G-36), then `graphic_memory` (issue #127, spec §11 G-37)."""

import re

DEV_TOOLS = ["snapshot_ui", "perform_menu_item", "cancel_sheet", "select_inspector_tab",
             "assistant_send", "assistant_answer", "play_preview", "graphic_memory"]

MARKER = re.compile(r"Frame Job agent server: framejob-dev-tools-compiled-in, (\d+) dev tools")


def dev_marker_count(log_path):
    """The dev-tool count the flag-on `devTools()` logged at startup, or None
    when the log holds no marker line (a Distribution build, or no log)."""
    try:
        with open(log_path, errors="replace") as handle:
            text = handle.read()
    except OSError:
        return None
    found = MARKER.findall(text)
    return int(found[-1]) if found else None

content.content:
pauses. While it plays,
`PlaybackTrial.swift` records each frame the compositor finished on the
document's key: its time, its compose time, and, with `digests: true`, the
SHA-256 of the destination buffer's rows (each row's first `width × 8`
bytes, 64RGBAHalf). It answers, keys in this order: `from`, `to`, `rate`,
`wall_seconds`, `frame_ticks` (f, the built composition's frame duration),
`frames_expected` (max(0, k1 − k0 + 1), k0 = ⌊from / f⌋ — ⌊seek_to / f⌋ with
`seek_to` — and k1 = ⌊(to − 1) / f⌋), `frames_composed` (the distinct ⌊t / f⌋
in [k0, k1] among the frames served), `composed_ratio` (3 places; 0 when none
were expected), `compose_ms {mean, p95, worst}` (nearest rank, over every
frame served), `seek_from` (only with `seek_to`), `stale_reached` (only with
`stale_ticks`: the ticks reported — all of them, or `[]` when the armed wait
ran out) and `digests` (only when asked: a tick string → SHA-256 hex).
Refused, each in its own sentence and before anything moves: `stale_ticks`
without `seek_to`, an empty `stale_ticks`, a negative tick, and
`stale_armed` without `stale_ticks`. Refused, each in its own sentence: a
project with no editor window and a preview with no item to play, changing
nothing, and a preview still seeking after 5 s, which it has paused. It ends
paused where the play reached. It is
`playback_prefetch_proof.py`'s instrument.
**`graphic_memory {pressure?}`** (issue #127, §11 G-37) answers the graphic
rasters' one memory budget and the frames a document keeps. It needs no
project and runs off the main thread. `pressure` — `"normal"`, `"warning"` or
`"critical"`, any other value refused in its own sentence before anything
moves — first sets a SIMULATED memory-pressure level, which holds against the
system's real events until the tool sets `"normal"`; that clears the
simulation and applies the last real level. It answers `physical_bytes`
(`ProcessInfo.physicalMemory`), `budget_bytes` (a quarter of it at normal, an
eighth at warning, 0 at critical), `pressure` (the level in force),
`held_bytes` (every session's rasters held ahead now), `held_peak_bytes` and
`held_peak_entries` (the highest totals since the last answer, which resets
them to the current ones), `kept_bytes` and `kept_frames` (the kept frames'
total and count, over every document), `kept_hits` (how many compositor
requests the kept frames have answered since launch), `ahead_bytes` (the kept
frames a background pass drew ahead that the compositor has not passed, §11
G-38), `ahead_evicted` (those a trim pushed out while still ahead, since the
last answer, which resets it to 0), `pass_activity` (whether a running
background pass holds the App Nap opt-out), `image_cache_bytes` (what the
engine's decoded-image cache of PNG and JPEG assets holds, §11 G-39) and
`image_cache_limit` (its limit: `budget_bytes / 16`, 0 under
`FrameJobGraphicImageCacheOff`). It is `graphic_memory_proof.py`'s,
`background_render_proof.py`'s and `image_cache_proof.py`'s instrument.

**The transport is spec §11 MC-1..MC-6** (road map 14,
`designs/adr/roadmap-14-agent-socket.md`): the server listens only on a Unix socket,
`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`, at every launch
(MC-1), bound by the first instance and only in its own `0700` `Agent`
subfolder the person owns (MC-2); an external client reaches it through
`framejob-mcp`, the bundle's stdio server (MC-3), which answers `initialize`
and `tools/list` without launching Frame Job and launches it in the background
on the first `tools/call` that finds no socket (MC-4); a tool call never
raises a modal question (MC-5); and `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` overrides the path,
which every proof sets (MC-6). The socket is bound at every launch
(`AgentServer+Socket.swift`) and is the only listener: road map 14's MC4
deleted the TCP one, its switch and MC-6's interim rule. A tool call decides
"may ask" where it hands work to the importer, so a person's own import
still asks while a call runs (MC-5). Settings' MCP section's Copy MCP
Command (MC-7) puts the `claude mcp add` line for the bundle's own
`framejob-mcp` on the clipboard; it is not an edit, so it has no tool.

The instance still shares its bundle's settings domain, so never perform a
menu item that persists a setting (the View menu's Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide
Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview Quality) from a script.

A Debug or Release build, never Distribution, also has dev-only tools over
MCP: `snapshot_ui` (a capture of the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the

`PlaybackTrial.swift` records each frame the compositor finished on the
document's key: its time, its compose time, and, with `digests: true`, the
SHA-256 of the destination buffer's rows (each row's first `width × 8`
bytes, 64RGBAHalf). It answers, keys in this order: `from`, `to`, `rate`,
`wall_seconds`, `frame_ticks` (f, the built composition's frame duration),
`frames_expected` (max(0, k1 − k0 + 1), k0 = ⌊from / f⌋ — ⌊seek_to / f⌋ with
`seek_to` — and k1 = ⌊(to − 1) / f⌋), `frames_composed` (the distinct ⌊t / f⌋
in [k0, k1] among the frames served), `composed_ratio` (3 places; 0 when none
were expected), `compose_ms {mean, p95, worst}` (nearest rank, over every
frame served), `seek_from` (only with `seek_to`), `stale_reached` (only with
`stale_ticks`: the ticks reported — all of them, or `[]` when the armed wait
ran out) and `digests` (only when asked: a tick string → SHA-256 hex).
Refused, each in its own sentence and before anything moves: `stale_ticks`
without `seek_to`, an empty `stale_ticks`, a negative tick, and
`stale_armed` without `stale_ticks`. Refused, each in its own sentence: a
project with no editor window and a preview with no item to play, changing
nothing, and a preview still seeking after 5 s, which it has paused. It ends
paused where the play reached. It is
`playback_prefetch_proof.py`'s instrument.
**`graphic_memory {pressure?}`** (issue #127, §11 G-37) answers the graphic
rasters' one memory budget and the frames a document keeps. It needs no
project and runs off the main thread. `pressure` — `"normal"`, `"warning"` or
`"critical"`, any other value refused in its own sentence before anything
moves — first sets a SIMULATED memory-pressure level, which holds against the
system's real events until the tool sets `"normal"`; that clears the
simulation and applies the last real level. It answers `physical_bytes`
(`ProcessInfo.physicalMemory`), `budget_bytes` (a quarter of it at normal, an
eighth at warning, 0 at critical), `pressure` (the level in force),
`held_bytes` (every session's rasters held ahead now), `held_peak_bytes` and
`held_peak_entries` (the highest totals since the last answer, which resets
them to the current ones), `kept_bytes` and `kept_frames` (the kept frames'
total and count, over every document), `kept_hits` (how many compositor
requests the kept frames have answered since launch), `ahead_bytes` (the kept
frames a background pass drew ahead that the compositor has not passed, §11
G-38), `ahead_evicted` (those a trim pushed out while still ahead, since the
last answer, which resets it to 0), `pass_activity` (whether a running
background pass holds the App Nap opt-out), `image_cache_bytes` (what the
engine's decoded-image cache of PNG and JPEG assets holds, §11 G-39) and
`image_cache_limit` (its limit: `budget_bytes / 16`, 0 under
`FrameJobGraphicImageCacheOff`). It is `graphic_memory_proof.py`'s,
`background_render_proof.py`'s and `image_cache_proof.py`'s instrument.

**The transport is spec §11 MC-1..MC-6** (road map 14,
`designs/adr/roadmap-14-agent-socket.md`): the server listens only on a Unix socket,
`~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Agent/agent.sock`, at every launch
(MC-1), bound by the first instance and only in its own `0700` `Agent`
subfolder the person owns (MC-2); an external client reaches it through
`framejob-mcp`, the bundle's stdio server (MC-3), which answers `initialize`
and `tools/list` without launching Frame Job and launches it in the background
on the first `tools/call` that finds no socket (MC-4); a tool call never
raises a modal question (MC-5); and `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` overrides the path,
which every proof sets (MC-6). The socket is bound at every launch
(`AgentServer+Socket.swift`) and is the only listener: road map 14's MC4
deleted the TCP one, its switch and MC-6's interim rule. A tool call decides
"may ask" where it hands work to the importer, so a person's own import
still asks while a call runs (MC-5). Settings' MCP section's Copy MCP
Command (MC-7) puts the `claude mcp add` line for the bundle's own
`framejob-mcp` on the clipboard; it is not an edit, so it has no tool.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Tutorials TU1b — the practice project, proved against the running app
(spec §11 TU-7).

    python3 tools/proof/practice_project_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock [--log PATH]

`--log` defaults to `<dir>/framejob.log`. A Debug or Release build (P2 uses
the dev tool `perform_menu_item`), FRESH for each run, with no other project
open: the rows write under `work/practice_project/`, wiped at the start. An
untitled copy is addressed only as the frontmost document, so the rows run in
this order:

- **T1** — no `Frame Job: ` line in the log (the startup parity check).
- **B1** — the instance's own `Contents/Resources/Practice Project.framejob`
  (its executable read through `lsof`, no MCP) holds exactly the files of
  `app/Resources/Practice/SHA256SUMS`, each with its digest.
- **O1** — `open_project {path: <that bundled package>}` is refused, and the
  refusal names `new_project` and `practice`.
- **P1** — `new_project {practice: true}`, then `get_project`: name "Practice
  Project", path null, `unsaved_changes` false, canvas 1280×720, three clips
  on one track at 0, 6 and 12 s, none with a `transition_in`, no
  `missing_media`, and every media path inside the bundled package's
  `media/`.
- **P2** — `perform_menu_item ["Help", "Tutorials", "Open Practice Project"]`
  opens one more editor window, and `get_project` (now that copy, the
  frontmost) answers the same three clips, named "Practice Project".
- **P3** — `render_frame` of P2's copy at 1, 7 and 13 s writes three PNGs,
  pairwise byte-different (Dawn, Sea, Night).
- **P4** — on P2's copy (no `project` argument): `set_audio` on its first
  clip (volume 0.5), then `save_project {path: work/practice_project/saved}`
  answers `saved` with `project.name` "saved"; the saved package's `media/`
  holds Dawn.mov, Sea.mov and Night.mov byte-equal to the bundle's; its
  `project.json` names each media at `<saved>/media/<file>`, none inside the
  app, with no bookmark. Then `close_project {project: <saved>, discard:
  true}`.
- **R1** — `open_project {path: <saved>}`: name "saved", no `missing_media`,
  every media path inside `<saved>/media/`, the first clip's volume 0.5;
  closed by its path. P1's copy, now the only document, is closed with
  `close_project {discard: true}`.
- **P5** — `new_project {practice: true, path: work/practice_project/direct}`
  answers `saved` with `project.name` "direct", and its package passes P4's
  `media/` and `project.json` checks; closed by its path.
- **N1** — the bundled package's files still equal `SHA256SUMS`, with no
  file added.

A name "saved" or "direct" is the file's name as AppKit's `displayName`
gives it: the stem, or the stem with `.framejob` where the host shows
extensions (`file_named`); what the rows refuse is "Practice Project" kept
after the save.

Rows print as `<ID> pass|fail — <detail>`, then `scores:`. Exit 0 iff no row
failed.
"""

import argparse
import hashlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import sys

# Spec: Tutorials TU2 — the model, the runner and Show Me, with no chrome

## Goal
Read `Tutorials.json` into typed tutorials and run one per editor window: needs, reveal, waits, variables, Back/Skip/Next/Exit and Show Me (tool and menu forms, Distribution-safe), driven over four dev tools and proved by `tutorial_proof.py` on the practice project. Fix TU1b's three review nits.

## Files
- `designs/spec/11-decisions/tutorials.md` — FIRST, before code: TU-8 (model + runner, Approach 1–6) and TU-9 (Show Me, Approach 7); TU-2 (8) gains "a menu Show Me's selector verdict in `inventory.json` is `none`, `sheet` or `window`".
- `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md` — TU-8, TU-9 rows; `tutorials.md` row's line count and summary.
- `designs/spec/07.9c-agent-graphics-dev-tools-transport.md` — the four tutorial dev tools; `select_inspector_tab`'s `visible_sections`. `designs/spec/README.md` — Lines cells for 07.9c and `11-decisions/`.
- `app/Sources/TutorialModel.swift` (new, ≤400) — `TutorialLibrary` and the step types; strict decode.
- `app/Sources/TutorialRunner.swift` (new, ≤400) — lifecycle, triggers, navigation, state answer.
- `app/Sources/TutorialWait.swift` (new, ≤400) — baselines, condition evaluation, the needs sentence.
- `app/Sources/TutorialVariables.swift` (new, ≤400) — resolving TU-2 (9)'s variables.
- `app/Sources/TutorialShowMe.swift` (new, ≤400) — Show Me's tool form (lane) and menu form.
- `app/Sources/InspectorReveal.swift` (new) — pure move out of `AgentServer+InspectorTab.swift` of `shownPane`, `scroll(to:)`, `clipPane` as `InspectorViewController` members (product code), plus `reveal` and `visibleSectionIDs`.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+InspectorTab.swift` — calls the moved members; answer gains `visible_sections`; description says so.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+Tutorials.swift` (new, wholly `#if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS`) — the four handlers and catalog rows.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+DevTools.swift` — four handler rows, `tutorial_step` in `devOffMainTools`, four rows appended to `devTools()` in order, doc lists.
- `app/Sources/UIMenu.swift` — narrow `#if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` so `Leaf`, `Lookup`, `selector(of:)`, `leaves`, `lookup`, `fillDynamic`, `validate`, `responders`, `target(for:window:)`, `isEnabled`, `textReadOnlySelectors` and `perform` compile in every build; `Verdict`, `Refusal`, `refusal(for:)`, `listing(window:)` stay flagged; header doc names the runner. No call site renamed.
- `app/Sources/EditorViewController.swift` (frozen, wiring only) — `var tutorialRunner: TutorialRunner?`; in `projectDidChange(_:)` after `refreshFromDocument`, `tutorialRunner?.documentDidChange(isLive:)`; in `playbackRateChanged(_:)`, `tutorialRunner?.playbackRateChanged(rate)`.
- `app/Sources/EditorViewController+Inspector.swift` — `inspectorPlayheadMoved()` first line `tutorialRunner?.trigger()`.
- `app/Sources/EditorViewController+Export.swift` — `beginExport` and `enqueueExport` call `tutorialRunner?.noteExportStarted()` after the job/sheet starts.
- `app/Sources/AgentServer+Export.swift` — inside the enqueue `onMain`, `self.editor(document)?.tutorialRunner?.noteExportStarted()`.
- `app/Sources/AgentLane.swift` — `releasingLock` doc: `tutorial_step` is a third caller. Doc only.
- `app/Sources/TutorialClipFacts.swift` — nit 1: `matches` takes a Bool only when `CFGetTypeID(wanted as CFTypeRef) == CFBooleanGetTypeID()` (via `TutorialJSON.isBool`).
- `app/Sources/MediaConsolidator.swift` — nit 3: `carriedPracticeFile` looks for `PracticeProject.packageName(for: url, in: directory)`, requiring it exists with the source's byte size.
- `docs/guide/canvas-and-layers.md` — Add a title step 1's wait becomes `{"clips": {"added": 1, "kind": "text"}, "selection": {"kind": "text"}}` (sentence unchanged).
- `tools/proof/tutorial_probe.swift` — 4th argument: a model-cases file; answer gains `model` and `filter_number_matches`.
- `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` — model cross-check, menu-verdict rule, nit 2, new mutants, docstring counts.
- `tools/proof/tutorial_fixtures/facts.json` (and `inventory.json` if a verdict is needed) — the `model` block and `filter_number_matches: false`.
- `tools/proof/tutorial_proof.py` (new) — the MCP proof.
- `tools/proof/dev_tools.py` — append the four names; docstring.
- `tools/proof/assistant_session_proof.py` — line 391's `== 8` becomes `== 12`.
- `tools/proof/README.md` — the "Tutorials checked" section's counts; a new "The tutorial runner" section after "The practice project".
- `docs/developing.md` — the dev-tool list (~line 314) names the four.
- `designs/tutorials.md` — the TU2 record under "Record" (numbers only as printed).

## Interfaces
```swift
enum TutorialJSON { static func isBool(_ v: Any) -> Bool; static func isInt(_ v: Any) -> Bool }  // isInt: NSNumber, not CFBoolean, integral
struct TutorialModelError: LocalizedError { let message: String }
struct TutorialLibrary {
    let pages: [TutorialPage]; let refused: [String: String]      // tutorial id → the model's reason
    static func decode(_ data: Data) throws -> TutorialLibrary     // throws on top level (not an object, format != 1, pages not a list)
    static func bundled() throws -> TutorialLibrary                // Bundle.main "Tutorials.json", memoised
    func tutorial(id: String) -> Tutorial?; var ids: [String] { get }   // guide order
}
struct TutorialPage { let page: String; let title: String; let tutorials: [Tutorial] }
struct Tutorial { let id, title, anchor: String; let needs: [String: Any]?; let steps: [TutorialStep] }
struct TutorialStep { let text: String; let reveal: TutorialReveal?; let spotlight: String?
    let wait: [TutorialCondition]; let showMe: [TutorialShowMe]; let optional: Bool }
struct TutorialReveal: Equatable { let tab: InspectorTab; let subTab: ClipSubTab?; let section: String? }
enum TutorialClipSet: String { case selection = "$selection", created = "$created" }
enum TutorialRangeEdge: String { case start, end }
enum TutorialCondition { case selection(min: Int, max: Int?, filter: [String: Any]), changed([String]),
    clips(added: Int, kind: String?), playheadInside(TutorialClipSet), rangeSet, rangeChanged(TutorialRangeEdge),
    sheetExport, exportStarted, playing }
enum TutorialShowMe { case tool(name: String, args: [String: Any]), menu(path: [String]) }

struct TutorialRefusal: Error { let sentence: String }
enum TutorialAdvance: String { case wait, next, skip }
struct TutorialShowMeOutcome { let step: Int; let ok: Bool; let error: String?; let results: [String] }  // results: each call's result text
final class TutorialRunner {
    static func start(_ tutorial: Tutorial, in editor: EditorViewController) throws -> TutorialRunner  // TutorialRefusal; installs, replacing
    func trigger(); func documentDidChange(isLive: Bool); func playbackRateChanged(_ rate: Float); func noteExportStarted()
    func next() throws; func back() throws; func skip() throws; func showMe() throws; func exit()   // TutorialRefusal
    var showMeRunning: Bool { get }; var offers: [String] { get }; func state() -> [String: Any]
}
struct TutorialBaseline { init(document: ProjectDocument) }   // selection (time-ordered), clip ids, range, per-path values
enum TutorialWait { static func needsSentence(_ needs: [String: Any]?, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> String? }
enum TutorialVariables { static func resolve(_ value: Any, selection: [UInt32], created: [UInt32],
    snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, playhead: Ticks) throws -> Any }   // TutorialRefusal
extension InspectorViewController { func reveal(_ r: TutorialReveal) -> String?   // nil, or the refusal sentence
    func visibleSectionIDs() -> [String] }
```
Dev tools (each also takes `project`, injected by `tool()`): `tutorial_start {id}` (main), `tutorial_state {}` (main), `tutorial_step {action: "show_me"|"next"|"back"|"skip"}` (off main), `tutorial_exit {}` (main). Every answer but a refusal is the state: `{ok, project, running}`, and when running also `id, title, step` (1-based), `steps, text, optional, wait` (bool), `show_me` (bool), `offers` (subset of `back, show_me, skip, next, exit` in that order), `spotlight, reveal` (`{tab, sub_tab, section}` or null), `reveal_refused, finished, show_me_running, last_show_me` (`{step, ok, error, results}` or null), `selection_at_start, created, completed` (`[{step, by}]`).

## Approach
1. **Model (TU-8 (1)).** Decode format 1; refuse per tutorial (into `refused`) any key, type or value outside TU-2 (2)–(9) — closed keys at every level, id pattern, filter keys/kinds, `min`/`max`, `range` exactly one, `sheet` "export", `true` literals, `reveal` against `InspectorTab`/`ClipSubTab`/`TutorialTargets.sections` homes, `spotlight` against `TutorialTargets`, show_me shape, `$`-strings/keys. Catalog, menu-bar, inventory and fixture-path checks stay the checker's (build time); one failing at run time is a refused Show Me.
2. **Start (TU-8 (2)).** One runner per editor window, `editor.tutorialRunner`; start replaces; Exit sets it nil and undoes nothing; closing the window ends it. Needs are checked against `document.editedProject.snapshot` with `TutorialClipFacts`; unmet → `TutorialRefusal(needsSentence)`: `This tutorial needs ` + (`a clip` | `a`/`an` `<kind> clip`) + (none | ` that ` + predicates) + `.`; predicates in `TutorialClipFacts.keys` order: `has sound`/`has no sound`, `has a picture`/`has no picture`, `meets the clip before it on its track`/`does not meet the clip before it on its track`, `has a transition in`/`has no transition in`; joined `p`, `p1 and p2`, `p1, p2 and p3`. E.g. "This tutorial needs a clip that has sound."
3. **Triggers (TU-8 (3)).** Committed document change and `viewStateDidChange` (the editor's hook; `isLive` ticks ignored), playhead moves, rate changes, `NSWindow.willBeginSheetNotification`/`didEndSheetNotification` on the editor's window (block observers removed in `deinit`), and `noteExportStarted`. No polling. The inspector tab is no trigger: no condition reads it. Each trigger schedules ONE coalesced evaluation on the next main turn (`DispatchQueue.main.async`, a pending flag), so the event that met a wait (T's selection, the inspector's rebuild, a sheet's attach) has finished first. A wait is evaluated only after a trigger since its step began — never at its start, so Back stays put. While a Show Me runs, evaluations are held; one runs after its last entry.
4. **Conditions (TU-8 (4)).** Baseline at step begin: selection ids, clip-id set, range, latches cleared. `selection`: count in [min, max] and every selected clip matches. `changed`: any clip selected at the step's start differs at any listed path from its start value (`editedProject.json` `clips`, dotted path, absent = `NSNull`, compared with `isEqual`; parsed clips cached per handle). `clips`: at least `added` ids now absent at start (of `kind`). `playhead inside`: start < playhead < end of any clip in the set. `range set`: non-nil; `changed`: that edge differs from start. `sheet`: `window.attachedSheet?.contentViewController is ExportSheetController`. `export_started`/`playing`: latched since step begin (rate ≠ 0). Met → advance in that evaluation.
5. **Variables (TU-8 (5)).** `$selection` = start selection; `$created` = ids added by the latest earlier step or earlier call of this Show Me that added any (per step begin the value is recorded; Back restores it); time order = start, ties front track first (`tracks.last` is front). `$time` span = earliest start to latest end; `middle` snapped with `ReelTime.snapToFrame`. `$track` front resolved per call.
6. **Navigation and reveal (TU-8 (6)).** Begin a step: baseline, then `inspector.reveal` (`select`, `selectClipSubTab` if offered, scroll; writes no preference); a refusal goes in `reveal_refused`, step still shown. Next only without wait; Skip only optional; Back from step > 1 or finished re-begins the previous step; after the last step `finished`. Each refused with a one-sentence `TutorialRefusal`.
7. **Show Me (TU-9).** Entries in order. Tool: resolve variables, `AgentLane.shared.submit(tool:argumentsJSON:document:askFirst:completion:)` pinned to the runner's document, `askFirst` answering `true` (the press is the ask), completion hopped to main (`DispatchQueue.main.async`; dropped if the runner was replaced). `isError` → stop, `error` = its text verbatim. Menu: `UIMenu.lookup` for the editor's window; missing → "The menu bar has no A ▸ B ▸ C."; no target or `isEnabled` false → "A ▸ B ▸ C is not available now."; else `UIMenu.perform` (its undo grouping); unhandled → "A ▸ B ▸ C was not handled." A failed Show Me leaves the step. Earlier entries' edits stay, each an ordinary undo step.
8. **Dev tools.** `AgentServer+Tutorials.swift`: `target(a)`; no editor window refused as `select_inspector_tab` does; unknown id refused naming `TutorialLibrary.ids`; a refused id answers the model's reason. `tutorial_step show_me`: `onMain { runner.showMe() }`, then `AgentLane.shared.releasingLock` polling `showMeRunning` on main every 50 ms up to 60 s (the assistant tools' precedent), then the state.
9. **Inspector move.** Pure move first, then `visible_sections` (ids whose frame intersects the clip view's visible rect, top to bottom) in the dev tool's answer.
10. **Checker.** Probe arg 4 is `{"guide": <extracted guide>, "mutants": {name: <document>}}`; answer `model: {guide: {id: null|reason}, mutants: {name: null|reason}}` and `filter_number_matches` (a practice clip's `matches` on JSON `{"has_sound": 1}`). Problems: a checker-accepted tutorial the model refused; a model mutant decoded; `filter_number_matches` true; empty/missing practice `media` (nit 2); a menu Show Me whose verdict is `modal`/`framework`. `MODEL_MUTANTS` = `unknown-spotlight`, `section-not-in-table`, `section-other-home`, `unknown-variable` plus new MUTANTS `unknown-step-key`, `selection-min-negative`, `range-both`, `sheet-other`, `optional-not-bool`, `kind-unknown`, built from the fixture page; the selftest also requires `check()` to refuse each. New selftest cases: those six, `model-guide-refused`, `model-mutant-accepted`, `filter-number`, `practice-media-empty`, `menu-verdict-modal`. The fixture CONTROL must decode in the real model.
11. **Proof `tutorial_proof.py <dir>/agent.sock`.** Each run on a fresh `new_project {practice: true}` closed with `close_project {discard: true}` (front document only). Rows: T1 log clean. P-<id> per tutorial as a person, after each action the step read and, on a reveal, `select_inspector_tab {}`'s tab, sub_tab and `visible_sections`: volume (`set_selection` Dawn, `set_audio` 0.5, `play_preview {seconds: 1}`); split (`set_selection` Dawn, `set_playhead` 3 s, `perform_menu_item` Clip ▸ Split); add_title (`add_track`, `add_text_clip` — still step 1 — `set_selection`, `set_text`, `set_video`); cross_dissolve (`set_selection` Sea, `perform_menu_item` Clip ▸ Transition ▸ Cross Dissolve, `set_transition_duration`); export (`set_range` start then end, `perform_menu_item` File ▸ Export…, `next`, `export` to `work/tutorial_proof/`, wait done, `cancel_sheet`). M-<id> by Show Me alone (show_me, else next, else skip), then `get_project`: Dawn volume 1.5; four clips, Dawn split at 3 s; a second track with a text clip "My first title" at y 300; Sea's `transition_in` cross dissolve, start moved; range [0, 3 s]. The export Show Me writes `~/Movies/Frame Job Tutorial.mp4`: the row FAILS without running if that file exists, waits for the export (id from `last_show_me.results`), then deletes only the file it made. C-<id> on `new_project {}`: four exact needs sentences; add_title starts, then exit. B1 Back stays put; S1 Skip; N1 Next refused on a wait step; E1 Exit leaves project and undo untouched; R1 refused tool Show Me (split step 3 after `set_playhead` 15 s: step stays, error non-empty, three clips); R2 greyed menu (cross_dissolve step 2 after `set_selection []`: exact sentence, no transition); U1 `undo` after the volume Show Me restores the volume, step stays 3, `redo` reapplies. `Rows <ID> pass|fail — <detail>`, then `scores:`; exit 0 iff none failed.
12. **Mutants (7)**, run once at the end: evaluate at step begin (B1); no Show Me hold (M-canvas.add_title); menu skips `isEnabled` (R2); `askFirst` false (M-export.range); failed Show Me advances (R1); needs unchecked (C rows); `AgentServer+Export` hook removed (P-export.range). Nit 3 has no instrument; stated in the record.

## Constraints
- `EditorViewController.swift` is frozen: the three wiring lines only. `AgentServer.swift` untouched (DevTools merges). New files ≤400 lines; `+Inspector` is 403, under 600.
- Dev tools follow `AgentServer+InspectorTab.swift`/`+Assistant.swift`; rows sit before `import_media` in `dev_tools.py` order (`op_argument_proof.py`, `assistant_session_proof.py` A0). `AssistantToolTable` withholds them via `devToolNames`.

    static func decode(_ data: Data) throws -> TutorialLibrary     // throws on top level (not an object, format != 1, pages not a list)
    static func bundled() throws -> TutorialLibrary                // Bundle.main "Tutorials.json", memoised
    func tutorial(id: String) -> Tutorial?; var ids: [String] { get }   // guide order
}

enum TutorialRangeEdge: String { case start, end }

    clips(added: Int, kind: String?), playheadInside(TutorialClipSet), rangeSet, rangeChanged(TutorialRangeEdge),

enum TutorialShowMe { case tool(name: String, args: [String: Any]), menu(path: [String]) }

struct TutorialRefusal: Error { let sentence: String }
enum TutorialAdvance: String { case wait, next, skip }

    func trigger(); func documentDidChange(isLive: Bool); func playbackRateChanged(_ rate: Float); func noteExportStarted()
    func next() throws; func back() throws; func skip() throws; func showMe() throws; func exit()   // TutorialRefusal
    var showMeRunning: Bool { get }; var offers: [String] { get }; func state() -> [String: Any]
}
struct TutorialBaseline { init(document: ProjectDocument) }   // selection (time-ordered), clip ids, range, per-path values
enum TutorialWait { static func needsSentence(_ needs: [String: Any]?, in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> String? }
enum TutorialVariables { static func resolve(_ value: Any, selection: [UInt32], created: [UInt32],
    snapshot: ProjectSnapshot, playhead: Ticks) throws -> Any }   // TutorialRefusal
extension InspectorViewController { func reveal(_ r: TutorialReveal) -> String?   // nil, or the refusal sentence
    func visibleSectionIDs() -> [String] }
```
Dev tools (each also takes `project`, injected by `tool()`): `tutorial_start {id}` (main), `tutorial_state {}` (main), `tutorial_step {action: "show_me"|"next"|"back"|"skip"}` (off main), `tutorial_exit {}` (main). ## Approach
1. **Model (TU-8 (1)).** Decode format 1; refuse per tutorial (into `refused`) any key, type or value outside TU-2 (2)–(9) — closed keys at every level, id pattern, filter keys/kinds, `min`/`max`, `range` exactly one, `sheet` "export", `true` literals, `reveal` against `InspectorTab`/`ClipSubTab`/`TutorialTargets.sections` homes, `spotlight` against `TutorialTargets`, show_me shape, `$`-strings/keys. Catalog, menu-bar, inventory and fixture-path checks stay the checker's (build time); one failing at run time is a refused Show Me.
2. **Start (TU-8 (2)).** One runner per editor window, `editor.tutorialRunner`; start replaces; Exit sets it nil and undoes nothing; closing the window ends it. Needs are checked against `document.editedProject.snapshot` with `TutorialClipFacts`; unmet → `TutorialRefusal(needsSentence)`: `This tutorial needs ` + (`a clip` | `a`/`an` `<kind> clip`) + (none | ` that ` + predicates) + `.`; predicates in `TutorialClipFacts.keys` order: `has sound`/`has no sound`, `has a picture`/`has no picture`, `meets the clip before it on its track`/`does not meet the clip before it on its track`, `has a transition in`/`has no transition in`; joined `p`, `p1 and p2`, `p1, p2 and p3`. E.g. "This tutorial needs a clip that has sound."
3. **Triggers (TU-8 (3)).** Committed document change and `viewStateDidChange` (the editor's hook; `isLive` ticks ignored), playhead moves, rate changes, `NSWindow.willBeginSheetNotification`/`didEndSheetNotification` on the editor's window (block observers removed in `deinit`), and `noteExportStarted`. No polling. The inspector tab is no trigger: no condition reads it. Each trigger schedules ONE coalesced evaluation on the next main turn (`DispatchQueue.main.async`, a pending flag), so the event that met a wait (T's selection, the inspector's rebuild, a sheet's attach) has finished first. A wait is evaluated only after a trigger since its step began — never at its start, so Back stays put. While a Show Me runs, evaluations are held; one runs after its last entry.
4. **Conditions (TU-8 (4)).** Baseline at step begin: selection ids, clip-id set, range, latches cleared. `selection`: count in [min, max] and every selected clip matches. `changed`: any clip selected at the step's start differs at any listed path from its start value (`editedProject.json` `clips`, dotted path, absent = `NSNull`, compared with `isEqual`; parsed clips cached per handle). `clips`: at least `added` ids now absent at start (of `kind`). `playhead inside`: start < playhead < end of any clip in the set. `range set`: non-nil; `changed`: that edge differs from start. `sheet`: `window.attachedSheet?.contentViewController is ExportSheetController`. `export_started`/`playing`: latched since step begin (rate ≠ 0). Met → advance in that evaluation.
5. **Variables (TU-8 (5)).** `$selection` = start selection; `$created` = ids added by the latest earlier step or earlier call of this Show Me that added any (per step begin the value is recorded; Back restores it); time order = start, ties front track first (`tracks.last` is front). `$time` span = earliest start to latest end; `middle` snapped with `ReelTime.snapToFrame`. `$track` front resolved per call.
6. **Navigation and reveal (TU-8 (6)).** Begin a step: baseline, then `inspector.reveal` (`select`, `selectClipSubTab` if offered, scroll; writes no preference); a refusal goes in `reveal_refused`, step still shown. Next only without wait; Skip only optional; Back from step > 1 or finished re-begins the previous step; after the last step `finished`. Each refused with a one-sentence `TutorialRefusal`.
7. **Show Me (TU-9).** Entries in order. Tool: resolve variables, `AgentLane.shared.submit(tool:argumentsJSON:document:askFirst:completion:)` pinned to the runner's document, `askFirst` answering `true` (the press is the ask), completion hopped to main (`DispatchQueue.main.async`; dropped if the runner was replaced). `isError` → stop, `error` = its text verbatim. Menu: `UIMenu.lookup` for the editor's window; missing → "The menu bar has no A ▸ B ▸ C."; no target or `isEnabled` false → "A ▸ B ▸ C is not available now."; else `UIMenu.perform` (its undo grouping); unhandled → "A ▸ B ▸ C was not handled." A failed Show Me leaves the step. Earlier entries' edits stay, each an ordinary undo step.
8. **Dev tools.** `AgentServer+Tutorials.swift`: `target(a)`; no editor window refused as `select_inspector_tab` does; unknown id refused naming `TutorialLibrary.ids`; a refused id answers the model's reason. `tutorial_step show_me`: `onMain { runner.showMe() }`, then `AgentLane.shared.releasingLock` polling `showMeRunning` on main every 50 ms up to 60 s (the assistant tools' precedent), then the state.
9. **Inspector move.** Pure move first, then `visible_sections` (ids whose frame intersects the clip view's visible rect, top to bottom) in the dev tool's answer.
10. **Checker.** Probe arg 4 is `{"guide": <extracted guide>, "mutants": {name: <document>}}`; answer `model: {guide: {id: null|reason}, mutants: {name: null|reason}}` and `filter_number_matches` (a practice clip's `matches` on JSON `{"has_sound": 1}`). Problems: a checker-accepted tutorial the model refused; a model mutant decoded; `filter_number_matches` true; empty/missing practice `media` (nit 2); a menu Show Me whose verdict is `modal`/`framework`. `MODEL_MUTANTS` = `unknown-spotlight`, `section-not-in-table`, `section-other-home`, `unknown-variable` plus new MUTANTS `unknown-step-key`, `selection-min-negative`, `range-both`, `sheet-other`, `optional-not-bool`, `kind-unknown`, built from the fixture page; the selftest also requires `check()` to refuse each. P-<id> per tutorial as a person, after each action the step read and, on a reveal, `select_inspector_tab {}`'s tab, sub_tab and `visible_sections`: volume (`set_selection` Dawn, `set_audio` 0.5, `play_preview {seconds: 1}`); split (`set_selection` Dawn, `set_playhead` 3 s, `perform_menu_item` Clip ▸ Split); add_title (`add_track`, `add_text_clip` — still step 1 — `set_selection`, `set_text`, `set_video`); cross_dissolve (`set_selection` Sea, `perform_menu_item` Clip ▸ Transition ▸ Cross Dissolve, `set_transition_duration`); export (`set_range` start then end, `perform_menu_item` File ▸ Export…, `next`, `export` to `work/tutorial_proof/`, wait done, `cancel_sheet`). C-<id> on `new_project {}`: four exact needs sentences; add_title starts, then exit.
